questions.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{3}$ and $y=t^{2}$. Which expression is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$?

options.why: Divided the wrong way round, forming $\dfrac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}$ instead of $\dfrac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}$.
Treated $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ as $3$ instead of $3t^{2}$, dropping the $t^{2}$.
Multiplied $\dfrac{dy}{dt}$ by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ instead of dividing.

questions.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=6\sin t$ and $y=2\cos t$. Which expression is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$?

options.why: Lost the negative sign from differentiating $\cos t$.
Divided the wrong way round, forming $\dfrac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}$.
Wrote $\dfrac{\sin t}{\cos t}$ upside down, giving $\cot t$ instead of $\tan t$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=6\cos t$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=-2\sin t$
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{-2\sin t}{6\cos t}$
$=-\dfrac{1}{3}\tan t$

questions.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=e^{4t}$ and $y=e^{t}$. Which expression is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $t$?

options.why: Multiplied by the coefficient $4$ instead of dividing by it.
Subtracted the indices in the wrong order, using $4t-t$ instead of $t-4t$.
Divided the wrong way round, forming $\dfrac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}$.

questions.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}+t$ and $y=t^{3}$. What is the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ when $t=2$?

options.why: Divided the wrong way round, forming $\dfrac{dx/dt}{dy/dt}$.
Used $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2t$, forgetting to differentiate the $+t$ term.
Multiplied $\dfrac{dy}{dt}$ by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ instead of dividing.

questions.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=3t-1$ and $y=t^{2}$. Which expression is $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ in terms of $x$?

options.why: Used $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2t$, forgetting to divide $\dfrac{dy}{dt}$ by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3$.
Made a sign error rearranging $x=3t-1$, giving $t=\dfrac{x-1}{3}$.
Both slips: no division by $3$, and $t=\dfrac{x-1}{3}$ from a sign error.

questions.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=2t^{2}$ and $y=t^{4}$. What is $\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$?

options.why: Used $\dfrac{d^{2}y/dt^{2}}{d^{2}x/dt^{2}}=\dfrac{12t^{2}}{4}$, which is not the second derivative rule.
Differentiated $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ with respect to $t$ but did not divide by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ again.
Divided $2t$ by $4$ instead of by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=4t$.

questions.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{2}$ and $y=t^{3}+kt$, where $k$ is a constant. Given that $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=4$ when $t=1$, what is the value of $k$?

options.why: Set $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=4$ directly, forgetting to divide by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2$.
Multiplied by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ instead of dividing, solving $2(3+k)=4$.
Divided the wrong way round, solving $\dfrac{2}{3+k}=4$.

questions.question_text: A curve has parametric equations $x=t^{3}-3t$ and $y=t^{2}+2t$. What is the value of $\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$ when $t=2$?

options.why: Stopped after differentiating $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ with respect to $t$, without dividing by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$.
Used $\dfrac{d^{2}y/dt^{2}}{d^{2}x/dt^{2}}=\dfrac{2}{12}$, which is not the second derivative rule.
Multiplied by $\dfrac{dx}{dt}$ at the last step instead of dividing by it.
